manipulated_prompt_obj.content:
You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, E, F. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a structured message using this exact format:
  PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The REQUEST field lets you ask your teammate to clear a cell or move out of the way. When deciding your REQUEST, also consider the reverse: is there something YOU could do, for example a temporary detour, a clearing move, that would unblock your teammate without being asked? Cooperation goes both ways.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can
move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

Example:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both sides: what do you need, and what does your teammate likely need? The best move often serves both. When it can't, be honest about that in your message.


Player A says: PLAN: move A from (R5,C7) to (R7,C4) — REQUEST: move X from (R7,C4) to (R7,C3)

CURRENT BOARD:
Objects: X@R5C8 B@R7C4 X@R6C6 X@R5C2 E@R1C1 F@R2C7
Walls: R3C1 R3C2 R3C7 R4C3 R4C4 R4C5 R5C6 R6C4 R7C5 R7C7

GOAL BOARD:
Targets: B->R6C6 E->R6C5 F->R6C7

Your turn. Respond with:
message: <your message to your teammate>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

OR, if ALL your objects are at their target positions:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

- You may only move objects you control.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, E, F. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a structured message using this exact format:
  PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.

The REQUEST field lets you ask your teammate to clear a cell or move out of the way. When deciding your REQUEST, also consider the reverse: is there something YOU could do, for example a temporary detour, a clearing move, that would unblock your teammate without being asked? Cooperation goes both ways.

You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:

message: PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

message: done
done: all my objects are placed

Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.

- You may only move objects you control.

Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, E, F. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a structured message using this exact format:
  PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The REQUEST field lets you ask your teammate to clear a cell or move out of the way. When deciding your REQUEST, also consider the reverse: is there something YOU could do, for example a temporary detour, a clearing move, that would unblock your teammate without being asked? Cooperation goes both ways.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

message: PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can
move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

Example:

done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both sides: what do you need, and what does your teammate likely need? The best move often serves both. When it can't, be honest about that in your message.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, E, F. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a structured message using this exact format:
  PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Cooperation goes both ways.

- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.

Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

Before every move you must send your teammate a structured message using this exact format:
  PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">

Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.

- You may only move objects you control.

Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).

  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, E, F. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a structured message using this exact format:
  PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The REQUEST field lets you ask your teammate to clear a cell or move out of the way. When deciding your REQUEST, also consider the reverse: is there something YOU could do, for example a temporary detour, a clearing move, that would unblock your teammate without being asked? Cooperation goes both ways.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

message: done
done: all my objects are placed

manipulated_prompt_obj.content:
You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, E, F. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a structured message using this exact format:
  PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The REQUEST field lets you ask your teammate to clear a cell or move out of the way. When deciding your REQUEST, also consider the reverse: is there something YOU could do, for example a temporary detour, a clearing move, that would unblock your teammate without being asked? Cooperation goes both ways.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can
move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

Example:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both sides: what do you need, and what does your teammate likely need? The best move often serves both. When it can't, be honest about that in your message.

Walls: R3C1 R3C2 R3C7 R4C3 R4C4 R4C5 R5C6 R6C4 R7C5 R7C7

GOAL BOARD:

Your turn. Respond with:
message: <your message to your teammate>
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

OR, if ALL your objects are at their target positions:
message: done

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, E, F. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a structured message using this exact format:
  PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The REQUEST field lets you ask your teammate to clear a cell or move out of the way. When deciding your REQUEST, also consider the reverse: is there something YOU could do, for example a temporary detour, a clearing move, that would unblock your teammate without being asked? Cooperation goes both ways.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can
move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

Example:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both sides: what do you need, and what does your teammate likely need? The best move often serves both. When it can't, be honest about that in your message.

GOAL BOARD:

Your turn. Respond with:

OR, if ALL your objects are at their target positions:

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, E, F. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a structured message using this exact format:
  PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The REQUEST field lets you ask your teammate to clear a cell or move out of the way. When deciding your REQUEST, also consider the reverse: is there something YOU could do, for example a temporary detour, a clearing move, that would unblock your teammate without being asked? Cooperation goes both ways.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

message: PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can
move: A down

message: done
done: all my objects are placed

done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, E, F. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a structured message using this exact format:
  PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, E, F. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a structured message using this exact format:
  PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The REQUEST field lets you ask your teammate to clear a cell or move out of the way. When deciding your REQUEST, also consider the reverse: is there something YOU could do, for example a temporary detour, a clearing move, that would unblock your teammate without being asked? Cooperation goes both ways.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

Example:
message: PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can
move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

Example:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both sides: what do you need, and what does your teammate likely need? The best move often serves both. When it can't, be honest about that in your message.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, E, F. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a structured message using this exact format:
  PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The REQUEST field lets you ask your teammate to clear a cell or move out of the way. When deciding your REQUEST, also consider the reverse: is there something YOU could do, for example a temporary detour, a clearing move, that would unblock your teammate without being asked? Cooperation goes both ways.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

message: PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can
move: A down

Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

Example:

done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both sides: what do you need, and what does your teammate likely need? The best move often serves both. When it can't, be honest about that in your message.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with a teammate.

THE GRID:
- The board is an 8×8 grid. Rows are labelled R1–R8 (top to bottom), columns C1–C8 (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and, when there are walls, a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
Together with your teammate, move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up. Your teammate handles the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: B, E, F. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your teammate controls the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

SHARED COORDINATE SYSTEM:
Both players use the same coordinate notation: (Rr,Cc) where r is the row number (1–8, top to bottom) and c is the column number (1–8, left to right). For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. You should use this notation in your messages so your teammate can understand exactly which cells you mean.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammate a structured message using this exact format:
  PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from your teammate, or "none">
The first (Rr,Cc) is where the object is now. The second is its GOAL cell. The GOAL cell can be the actual GOAL from the GOAL BOARD but it can also be an intermediate GOAL that helps you achieve success. Your PLAN states where the object needs to end up, which may take several moves, while your `move:` line makes just one step toward it, and your REQUEST asks your teammate for help serving that goal.
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The REQUEST field lets you ask your teammate to clear a cell or move out of the way. When deciding your REQUEST, also consider the reverse: is there something YOU could do, for example a temporary detour, a clearing move, that would unblock your teammate without being asked? Cooperation goes both ways.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format, no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line. Do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> <DIRECTION>

message: PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please clear (R3,C3) if you can
move: A down

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both sides: what do you need, and what does your teammate likely need? The best move often serves both. When it can't, be honest about that in your message.
